- User base: core customers in EU, small support/admin access from APAC (~5% traffic).
- Latency target: sub-150ms p95 for Gen API in main EU region (NL/AMS preferred).

Attachments: EuroHealth-initial-requirements.pdf (your notes from discovery)

Next steps I propose: I will align with our infra and security leads on Private VPC feasibility and a Dedicated fallback architecture (for burst capacity). Goal: get you a short proposal + timeline by Friday.

Cheers,

Diego — thanks for the clear notes. Confirmations below and a couple of clarifications.

1) Residency: Persistent data (logs, model inputs/outputs) must remain in the EU at all times. Ephemeral in-memory processing in non-EU is acceptable only if there is an explicit, auditable control and data is not persisted. Given regulatory counsel, our preference is Private VPC or an EU-dedicated hosted region with contractual guarantees and controls.
2) Network contact: cc'd Sofia (our infra lead) — she will share a ticketing contact / network owner.
3) Compliance artifacts: please include SOC2 report, encryption at rest/in transit details, and any data-flow diagrams showing control points.

Additional note: we have a small user base in APAC that must be supported; cross-region routing is fine for routing requests, but any log replication or backups must be EU-only.

Attaching: eurohealth-security-extract.pdf (excerpt from our questionnaire)

If you can outline a pilot approach (minimum viable deployment) and an estimated timeline that would be great — propose next call with Sofia and our procurement lead the week after next.

Diego — quick notes after reviewing:

Recommended approach (scoped to their constraints):
1) Pilot on Private VPC in eu-west-1 (Amsterdam) with VPC peering: keeps all persistent storage in EU; we can configure logging to an EU-only object store with KMS keys tied to their account.
2) Burst strategy: use a Dedicated pool in the same region as an autoscale-burst target with warm standby nodes (reserved but idled) — avoids cross-region fallback. That meets their 200 QPS spikes without replicating data.
3) Contracts: we will need a residency addendum (data location + no cross-region backups) — legal can draft; expect 2–3 weeks review.
4) On-prem option: possible but requires PS engagement (4–8 weeks integration) and separate procurement. Recommend Private VPC + Dedicated-burst as shortest path to production.

Ops notes/questions to confirm with customer:
- Exact token distribution (you already provided averages; need 95p length if available).
- Any retention policy shorter than our default 30 days? (they may require 0-day retention for some datasets).
- Network constraints: do they allow egress to our control plane endpoints in the US? If not, we have a private control plane option but that'll increase lead time.

I can draft the pilot architecture and an estimated timeline: infra build (2–3 weeks), VPC peering + testing (1–2 weeks), pilot validation (1 week). Total: 4–6 weeks for pilot assuming timely network + legal responses.

Marissa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Alex / Sofia — thanks for the fast replies and for sharing the security extract. Per internal review, here is a pragmatic path forward: 

Proposed pilot (minimum viable):
- Deployment: Private VPC in eu-west-1 (Amsterdam).
- Data: all persistent storage/logging to remain in EU with customer-managed KMS. Ephemeral processing may transit non-EU control plane but no persistence.
- Burst handling: Dedicated reserved pool in eu-west-1 for warm standby capacity to absorb spikes to ~200 QPS. No cross-region replication.
- Timeline (estimates): infra + VPC setup 2–3 weeks; network peering & security testing 1–2 weeks; pilot validation 1 week => 4–6 weeks total.

Requested from you to move forward:
1) Sofia: network owner contact + firewall ticket to start peering (we can draft the template).
2) Procurement: confirm billing owner and PO process.
3) Compliance: indicate if 0-day retention is needed for any data class; if so, we will document controls and adjust scope.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-proposal.pdf (pilot architecture + estimate).

If that sounds good, let's lock a 30-min alignment next Tuesday (Sofia + procurement + Marissa on our side). I'll send a calendar invite once I hear availability.

Thanks — happy to clarify anything.

Diego
